definitions.explanation: A mild feeling of hunger between meals, not enough to warrant a full meal but enough to want a small snack.

examples.japanese: {小腹|こばら}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{空|す}いた⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦おにぎり→おにぎり：04956_onigiri⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{一|ひと}つ→一つ：02948_hitotsu⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I was a bit peckish, so I ate one rice ball.

examples.japanese: {小腹|こばら}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{空|す}いた{時|とき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{食|た}べられる→食べる：00396_taberu⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧、カバン⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦お{菓子|かし}→お菓子：02852_okashi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れている→入れる：01098_ireru⟧。
examples.english: I keep snacks in my bag so I can eat when I get a little hungry.

notes:
Literally 'small belly' (⟦{小|こ}→小〜：00240_ko⟧ small + ⟦{腹|はら}→腹：02165_hara⟧ belly/stomach). Used almost exclusively in the expression {小腹|こばら}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{空|す}く (to be slightly hungry). The ⟦{小|こ}→小〜：00240_ko⟧ prefix softens the degree, distinguishing it from full-on hunger.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {小腹|こばら}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{空|す}く: to be a little hungry
- {小腹|こばら}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{空|す}いた{時|とき}: when you're a bit peckish
- {小腹|こばら}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{満|み}たす→満たす：09889_mitasu⟧: to satisfy a small hunger

USAGE:
This word is strongly associated with snacking culture. It describes the feeling that leads you to eat a light snack (⟦{軽食|けいしょく}→軽食：15709_keishoku⟧) or buy something from a convenience store between meals. Very common in advertising for snack foods.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{空腹|くうふく}→空腹：06532_kuufuku⟧: hunger, empty stomach — stronger hunger, more formal
- ⟦お{腹|なか}→お腹：00805_onaka⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{空|す}く: to be hungry — the general, everyday expression
- ⟦{腹|はら}ぺこ→腹ぺこ：15601_harapeko⟧: starving, famished — casual, emphasizes strong hunger
